title: How can a wrong press be cancelled?
description: A child on the ground floor presses plus three by mistake and needs the lift to come back. The press that cancels it is found by moving the same number of floors the other way, and the two presses are added to give zero. Keeko thinks the mistake is fixed by pressing plus three again, and the lift rising to floor plus six breaks that doubt.
teaching_notes: One idea: a press is cancelled by the press of the same size in the other direction, and the two presses add to zero. Watch for students who add more of the same press.

source: On the ground floor, Basant is in a great hurry and by mista
video_script.why: A child learns that a press is cancelled by pressing the same number of floors the other way, which is the idea of an inverse.
video_script.substitution: the book's own lift on the ground floor, with a wrong plus three press and the press that cancels it
video_script.anchor: {{NAME_2}} on the ground floor of {{NAME_10}}, having pressed plus three by mistake
video_script.wrong_move: adds another press of the same kind, so the lift goes even higher
video_script.payoff_line: Moving the same number of floors the other way cancels a press.

final_answer.spoken: press minus three, because plus three and minus three make zero

names.{{NAME_2}}: pressed plus three by mistake on the ground floor and cancelled it with minus three
names.{{NAME_10}}: the multi-storey block of floors above and below the ground, used as the model for integers

never_show: the cancelling press before the answer
maths_rules: +3 takes the lift from the ground floor up three floors to the Book Store.
−3 takes it down three floors, back to the ground floor.
video_script.design: One idea: the same floors the other way cancel a press. One lift picture throughout; the two movements are drawn as arrows on one line. Keeko's doubt is broken by the lift rising to floor plus six.

<bookmark mark='hurry'/>{{NAME_2}} is in a great hurry and presses plus three by mistake.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What can {{NAME_2}} do to cancel it and stay on the ground floor?

<bookmark mark='stay'/>To stay on the ground floor, the lift must end where it began.

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, {{NAME_2}} is on the ground floor and has pressed plus three by mistake.

marks.find: the line To find is written under Given

narration: <bookmark mark='see'/>Step one, see where plus three takes the lift.
<bookmark mark='book'/>It goes up three floors, to the Book Store.

<bookmark mark='write'/>That is three floors down, which is minus three.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>{{NAME_2}} cancels the mistake by pressing minus three.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Moving the same number of floors the other way cancels a press.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the lift
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble says press +3 again; the lift is drawn rising from +3 to +6; the bubble is struck through

marks.higher: the lift rises from floor +3 to floor +6

beats.colours: warning colour for the struck bubble
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is to press plus three again, because adding more fixes the mistake.
<bookmark mark='higher'/>But another plus three takes the lift to floor plus six, even higher than before.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Going higher never brings it back, so the next press must go the other way.
